reply:
No. HttpOnly protects cookies from script access. It has zero effect on localStorage. They are separate storage mechanisms.

A JWT in localStorage is still readable by any script running on the page. An HttpOnly flag on *other* cookies doesn't change that. XSS doesn't need to "break" anything—it just reads localStorage directly:

```javascript
// This works inside any script, HttpOnly cookies or not
const token = localStorage.getItem('jwt');
```

The concrete cost: stolen JWT = attacker can make requests as that user until the token expires or you revoke it.

You need either:
1. Move the JWT to an HttpOnly cookie (works if your API accepts cookies instead of Bearer headers), or
2. Keep it in localStorage and accept the XSS risk, relying on other defenses (CSP, dependency auditing, input sanitization).

What does your API currently accept—Bearer header, or can it take a cookie?
